subject: Atlas Finance - Auth & Org Controls: handoff and implementation plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@atlasfinance.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@atlasfinance.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 04 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas Finance - Auth & Org Controls: handoff and implementation plan

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for choosing Redwood for inference. Per our kickoff, I’m starting the implementation handoff focused on enterprise access controls so engineering can schedule work next week. Attached is a short checklist and our suggested SCIM attribute mapping to accelerate the SCIM integration.

High-level asks for this phase (please see the attached checklist for owners & deadlines):
- Confirm IdP type & metadata (SAML 2.0 / OIDC) and provide test metadata or a temporary test IdP endpoint.
- SCIM: do you want group sync only, user + group, or both? Provide the primary email attribute we should map.
- IP allowlists: confirm whether you require our public egress IPs to be allowlisted or if you’ll place traffic behind your NAT gateway. If you need static egress IPs, we’ll provide the Dedicated pool addresses.
- Service accounts: confirm which Redwood services should run under dedicated service accounts vs. system-managed accounts and whether you need least-privilege RBAC.
- Org policies: share any naming conventions, org unit structures, or retention constraints that should be enforced at provisioning time.

Planned timeline suggestion:
- Discovery & IdP test access: Apr 5–7
- SCIM test sync & mapping: Apr 8–12
- IP allowlist / network validation: Apr 9–13
- Final validation & go-live: Apr 15

If that looks good, I’ll create a mutual action plan and assign owners. I’ve looped Jordan (CS lead) and Grace (security engineering) for technical follow-ups.

Attachments: atlas_enterprise_scim_spec.pdf, redwood_sso_checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
From: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@atlasfinance.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@atlasfinance.com>, Atlas Finance IT <it@atlasfinance.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Apr 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Finance - Auth & Org Controls: handoff and implementation plan

Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the clear list and timeline. Quick answers below so your team can start:

IdP: We use Okta (SAML 2.0). I can provision a test app and share the metadata XML by EOD Apr 5.

SCIM: We want user + group sync. Primary identifier is userPrincipalName (UPN), but email is authoritative in some cases; we can map UPN -> externalId and email -> email.

IP allowlists: We need your public egress IPs for any webhooks the platform calls back to us. For agent callbacks we’ll whitelist Redwood egress IPs. For admin console access, we’ll restrict to our corporate VPN ranges.

Service accounts: We prefer dedicated service accounts for API integrations. List the minimum scopes you need and we’ll create them in our IAM.

Org policies: Our main requirement is that SCIM-created users land in the OU path "/Engineering/AI-Integrations" and retention defaults to 2 years for audit logs.

We have a preferred time for the discovery call: Apr 6, 10:00am PT. Can you confirm?

Thanks,
Samantha Ross
Director, IT Operations
Atlas Finance
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 07:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Finance - Auth & Org Controls: handoff and implementation plan

Looping in a few technical questions ahead of the call so we can be efficient: 

1) Samantha said Okta / SAML. Do we need to support just SP-initiated SSO first, or will Atlas attempt IdP-initiated flows for admin users during testing?

2) For SCIM attribute mapping: please confirm which attributes Atlas expects for these fields: employeeType, department, manager (distinguishedName?), and whether email verification flags are required. If they use UPN as externalId, we need to know whether UPN sometimes differs from email.

3) Service accounts / API keys: we’ll propose two service accounts — one "scim-provisioner" scoped to user/group write operations and one "webhook-listener" for callbacks (read-only user info). Will Atlas accept scoped API keys, or do they need OAuth client credentials?

4) IP ranges: Samantha asked for public egress IPs. For Dedicated we have fixed pool addresses; for Hosted we publish a set of egress ranges that may rotate. Which environment is Atlas planning to use? (Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC)

I’ll prepare a Marshalled checklist and a short runbook for the discovery call (IdP metadata walk-through, SCIM mapping table, and test scenarios).

—Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Ross <samantha.ross@atlasfinance.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@atlasfinance.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Apr 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas Finance - Auth & Org Controls: handoff and implementation plan

Samantha — confirmed for Apr 6, 10:00am PT. Calendar invite sent. Below is the mutual action plan (short) we’ll review on the call; I’ll update the shared Confluence doc after the meeting with assigned owners and links.

Mutual action plan (initial):
- Apr 5: Atlas provides Okta metadata XML and test account provisioning (Samantha) — DONE/IN PROGRESS
- Apr 6: Discovery call — Confirm flow types, SCIM attribute mapping, and network constraints (All)
- Apr 7–9: Redwood prepares SCIM test connector, draft attribute map, and scoped service account request (Dev)
- Apr 9: Atlas provides dedicated service accounts + OU mapping confirmation (Samantha / IT)
- Apr 10–12: Test sync runs; fix mapping issues and validate deprovisioning behavior (Dev + Atlas IT)
- Apr 13: Network validation (Atlas adds Redwood egress IPs to allowlist)
- Apr 15: Final validation & go-live (All)

Action items for this week (owners):
- Samantha: Share Okta metadata and create test Okta app (by EOD Apr 5)
- IT (Atlas): Create one scoped service account for SCIM and one for webhooks (by Apr 9)
- Dev: Draft SCIM attribute map and share test endpoints (by Apr 7)
- Grace: Review any org policies that may require retention/archival changes (by Apr 9)

Notes:
- If Atlas prefers Dedicated for static IPs, we can provision a dedicated pool; that will change the procurement timeline and require a short Signature/PO (we’ve added the deal id to the DocuSign link).
- We’ll need a screenshot of your Okta assignment page if you use app-level assignment policies (helps with group sync troubleshooting).

I’ll upload the checklist and the draft mapping to the Confluence link after the call. Thanks everyone — see you at 10.

Best,
Hannah
